genZNote: Diagnosed mostly by blood test, not culture, because this organism takes its sweet time growing on a plate.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Blood of domestic and feral cats, especially kittens
habitat.hostAssociation: Zoonotic — cats are the primary reservoir; cat fleas transmit the organism among cats
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Primarily host-associated; transmitted to humans via cat scratch/bite (flea feces contamination of claws/mouth)

microscopy.appearance: Small pleomorphic bacilli visualized in lymph node or skin biopsy tissue with silver staining
microscopy.arrangement: Single cells, often clustered in tissue

culture.media: Enriched blood-based media (e.g., chocolate agar); requires prolonged incubation
culture.growthCharacteristics: Fastidious, slow-growing (can take 2-6 weeks) — culture is rarely used clinically
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, rough, adherent colonies after prolonged incubation

identificationClues: History of cat scratch/bite with regional tender lymphadenopathy in an otherwise well patient
Diagnosis relies primarily on serology (antibody titers) rather than culture, given how slow-growing/fastidious the organism is
Warthin-Starry silver stain demonstrates organisms in affected lymph node or skin tissue
Bacillary angiomatosis (vascular skin/organ lesions) is a distinct presentation in HIV/immunocompromised patients

diseases: Cat scratch disease — regional lymphadenopathy near the scratch/bite site, usually self-limited in immunocompetent hosts
Bacillary angiomatosis — vascular proliferative skin and visceral lesions in HIV/AIDS or other immunocompromised patients
Rare cases of endocarditis (culture-negative endocarditis is a classic association)
virulenceFactors: Ability to invade and persist within endothelial cells and erythrocytes
Induces vascular proliferation (angiogenesis), particularly relevant to bacillary angiomatosis in immunocompromised hosts
clinicalImportance.transmission: Cat scratch or bite (cat fleas maintain transmission among cats); rarely, flea bites directly to humans
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common causes of chronic regional lymphadenopathy in children and young adults with cat exposure; a classic (though uncommon) cause of culture-negative infective endocarditis
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Serology is the mainstay of diagnosis — culture is rarely positive due to the organism's fastidious, slow growth, so a negative culture does not exclude the diagnosis

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Fastidious — rarely cultured; diagnosis by serology
examFacts.importantDisease: Cat scratch disease; bacillary angiomatosis in HIV/immunocompromised patients
examFacts.importantTest: Serology (IgG/IgM titers); Warthin-Starry stain of tissue; PCR
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A cat-and-flea-transmitted organism causing regional lymphadenopathy in healthy hosts and vascular bacillary angiomatosis in the immunocompromised — a classic cause of culture-negative endocarditis

sources.name: CDC — Healthy Pets, Healthy People: Cat Scratch Disease
